newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded for first day since July 8.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded for first day since July 8.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures did not trade on Monday, although there was an Exchange for Physical (EFP) of 95 lots done in front month August, which rolls off the screen on Tuesday.

Monday was the first blank day since July 8. Futures volumes have been generally high since then. Last week 1,055 lots traded at an average of 211 lots a day, and the week before the total was 1,475 at an average 295 lots a day.
A futures broker pointed out that one major player which has done a lot of futures trade over the last two weeks has "cooled off" having accomplished what it needed to.
"It shows what happens when one or two major players pull out," he said. "The rest do nothing."
He added that after some weeks of rising prices, especially in the winter, the futures market "may be in for a bit of a correction."
Front month August was bid at 9.425 pence a therm and offered at 9.50 pence at the close, and there were bids and offers posted on all 12 contract months.
